implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the forwarding half of the pattern into the language: `class Cached(real: Image) : Image by real` makes the compiler generate every interface member as a call to the delegate, and only the operations whose access you control are overridden - the classic hand-written proxy class is normally unnecessary. The virtual-proxy half is also built in: `by lazy { ... }` defers and memoizes a property (synchronized by default, LazyThreadSafetyMode selects publication or no-safety), and Delegates.observable/vetoable cover smart-reference concerns. Write the explicit forwarding class only when the delegate must be rebindable at runtime (the `by` delegate is fixed at construction), when the proxy must expose a different type, or when the forwarded surface must be restricted.
pitfalls: The `by` delegate is stored once at construction and cannot be swapped; rebinding (SimpleDelegator.__setobj__-style) requires an explicit wrapper with a mutable field.
Members overridden in the delegating class are not called from the delegate's own internal calls: the delegate keeps calling its own implementations, so self-calls bypass the proxy.
lazy is synchronized by default - fine for correctness, a cost in hot paths; LazyThreadSafetyMode.NONE trades the guarantee away, and an initializer that throws is retried on the next access.
